management_notes: Management alignment and track record remain difficult to independently assess. The company IR site (churchillresources.com) continues to return HTTP 403 on datacenter IP fetches — a pattern consistent across all daily runs since at least June 2026. GlobeNewsWire RSS for the organisation also returned 403 on the July 25, 2026 run. The April 2026 interim MD&A (extracted 2026-05-14) confirms active filing cadence and an ongoing 2026 field program at Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond. A leadership transition was announced in late June / early July 2026 (flagged in a July 8, 2026 search snippet; executive appointment details have not been confirmed due to persistent 403s on press-release pages). No insider ownership schedule, biographical detail, or compensation disclosure has been accessible to date. Score of 2 maintained: continuity of operations and active drill program are positive signals; leadership transition creates uncertainty; insider alignment cannot be scored above a floor without confirmable data.
geology_notes: Churchill Resources holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine (Frost Cove / Black Raven property) in central Newfoundland and has expanded its district land position through the March 2026 Golden Baie option (39,925 ha, TSXV-approved March 27, 2026) and a Black Raven LOI. Confirmed geological highlights from accessible disclosures: (1) FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove — validated after the May 2026 data-correction release that downgraded the broader initial assay dataset; (2) a second new polymetallic system at southern Frost Cove / Black Raven yielding 7.25% Sb over 1.98m; (3) a 20-vein Au-Ag-Mo-Pb-Zn swarm at Pomley Cove Pond with surface channel results including 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag near the Frost Cove mine portal; (4) zinc grab samples at Black Raven reaching 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn with associated Au, Ag, and Pb. As of July 25, 2026, nine 2026 drill holes completed at Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond (reported as of July 13) remain without confirmed public assay release — neither IR site nor GlobeNewsWire was accessible to confirm whether results have been posted. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; its first 60 pages yielded no compliant resource estimate. Resource fields are null. Score of 3 reflects confirmed high-grade multi-commodity mineralisation across a consolidated NL property package, constrained by absence of a compliant resource estimate and pending assay results.
capital_notes: Per the April 29, 2026 interim MD&A (extracted 2026-05-14): 316,681,940 shares issued and outstanding; 342,756,940 shares fully diluted. Dilutive instruments: 2,625,000 warrants and 23,450,000 options; strike prices and expiry dates were not extractable from the MD&A summary table. The option pool (23.45M) represents approximately 7.4% of issued shares — elevated for a pre-resource junior. No flow-through tranches were detected in the April 2026 MD&A extraction. However, CRI has conducted flow-through financings in prior years as is common for small-cap NL explorers; any post-April 2026 flow-through issuance would not yet be reflected in the current extracted data. A $700K private placement was flagged in a July 8, 2026 press-release snippet (source blocked at 403); terms — share count, pricing, and warrant attachment — remain unconfirmed. If structured as a unit financing, this placement likely issued additional shares and warrants not yet reflected in the April cap-table. Score of 2 reflects the structurally heavy 316.7M basic share count for a pre-resource junior, an incomplete instrument-level detail preventing full dilution quantification, and an unconfirmed post-April financing.
catalyst_notes: Macro catalyst: China's September 2024 antimony export controls restricted supply from the dominant global producer and sustained government urgency across Canada, the US, the EU, and Australia for domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains. Antimony is named in Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and on the US Defense Production Act designated minerals list, making Foxtrot a credible candidate for NRCan/provincial grant support and strategic partnership interest. This macro tailwind remains durable as of July 25, 2026. Company-specific catalyst: nine 2026 drill holes completed at Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond as of July 13; assay results described as expected imminently at that date. As of July 25 (twelve days later), no results headline has been confirmed via accessible web sources — either results remain in the lab or were released but are inaccessible from datacenter IPs. If released, positive assays would be the most significant geological update since the May 2026 correction and could represent a re-rating catalyst. Planned Golden Baie exploration (airborne geophysics, trenching, drilling) adds a second pipeline of future news. Score of 3: durable macro tailwind plus imminent company drill catalyst, offset by inability to confirm release status of pending assays.
acquisition_notes: No NI 43-101 resource estimate is available to support a P/NAV calculation or comparables-based acquisition analysis. NAV per share cannot be derived. Strategic acquisition interest in non-Chinese antimony development assets in Tier-1 jurisdictions remains elevated following China's export controls. A past-producing property in Newfoundland, now with confirmed high-grade vein systems and multiple satellite targets across an expanded land position, would command a jurisdictional premium in any strategic transaction — particularly with Canadian and allied government interest in domestic critical mineral supply chains. However, without a defined resource, a potential acquirer has no tonnage-and-grade basis to anchor a bid beyond speculative exploration upside. The expanded land package (Golden Baie, Black Raven) increases strategic optionality but adds deal complexity. Score of 2: elevated strategic interest that cannot be monetised into a defensible acquisition thesis without a resource estimate.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine in central Newfoundland and has assembled a multi-property district position (Frost Cove/Black Raven, Golden Baie, Pomley Cove Pond) during a period of structurally elevated antimony prices and Western-government urgency over non-Chinese supply chains. The confirmed geological highlights — 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove (corrected, validated), 7.25% Sb over 1.98m at a second polymetallic system, 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag at Pomley Cove Pond veins, and up to 12.11% Zn grab samples at Black Raven — establish a credible multi-commodity exploration story across the consolidated land package. Nine 2026 drill holes were completed as of July 13; as of July 25, twelve days later, no results headline has been confirmed via accessible sources. If positive assays are released, they represent the primary near-term re-rating catalyst. The fundamental constraints on conviction remain unchanged: no NI 43-101 compliant resource estimate exists, a recent leadership transition adds management uncertainty, and the 316.7M basic share count (342.8M fully diluted) is heavy for a pre-resource junior. A $700K private placement announced in early July 2026 remains unconfirmed in terms. Capital-table detail (strike prices, expiry dates on all instruments) is incomplete. Maintain WATCH at low confidence: the strategic positioning in critical minerals with confirmed high-grade multi-commodity discovery platform justifies continued monitoring, but the absence of a compliant resource, pending assay uncertainty, and persistent data opacity prevent a higher conviction rating.
